texts: On day 301 of Year 1, the keepers of the Harbor Row carried the silken threads to Cauldron Hall.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the three cauldrons.
Mire-essence formed in the three cauldrons by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in four clay vessels.
The keepers of the Harbor Row drew the stored mire-essence at sundown.
Tessa Brae collected thirty of the fallen feathers at the base of the cliff in the morning.
Tessa Brae added the feathers to the feather bin.
Bevin Coombe took feathers from the feather bin.
Bevin Coombe scattered the ground feathers around the Stilllight Lantern at sundown.
The ground feathers warded the Stilllight Lantern against wraiths.
No wraith approached the Stilllight Lantern that night.

q1_issues.issue: "that night" is encoded only as the day-part (Time (sk_approach $x) night); the anaphoric-time term-propagation rule also requires copying the antecedent's stated day-level terms — (Day 301) and (Year 1) — onto the new event.

q2_gaps: day-of-year date numbering ("day 301 of Year 1") — the (Day <n>) term is specified as a calendar day paired with a month, so a day index with no month has no distinct encoding

stacked locative PPs whose inner object is a bare mass noun ("boiled … in sea-water in the three cauldrons") — the stacked-"in" rule is stated only for a second "in <Place>" on a place NP, and a bare mass constant has no witness to carry an entity-side position atom, leaving two co-equal Location atoms on one event as the only route

agent-nominalization taking an of-phrase ("the keepers of the Harbor Row") — it falls outside the nominalization-oblique rule's stated scope (act/result/quality nouns) yet passes that rule's verb-paraphrase test, while the Possession genitive is scoped to relational nouns with no underlying verb
review.notes: The partitive shape for "thirty of the fallen feathers", the "by evening" TimeAtMost bound, the participle-modifier distribution rules for fallen/ground, the material-adjective vs noun-modifier split (silken_thread exposes silken, clay_vessel does not expose clay), and the strength-0 rule with its "no" QuantifierPhrase companion are all correct. Witness indexing is clean — the definite superset sk_feather_1 stays distinct from the later indefinite sk_feather_2.

issues.reason: The term-propagation rule's own fallback licenses the bare day-part — "If the antecedent's day is unknown, emit just the day-part" — and by the coreference rule's recency test the salient antecedent time is the sundown scattering, which carries no day-level terms; copying (Day 301)/(Year 1) forward across the intervening "in the morning" would assert a date the text never gives the feather strand.

gaps_confirmed: Day-of-year dating ("day 301 of Year 1"): (Day <n>) is specified as a calendar day paired with a month, so a day index with no month has no distinct encoding.

Stacked locative PPs whose inner object is a bare mass noun ("boiled ... in sea-water in the three cauldrons"): the stacked-"in" rule is stated only for a second "in <Place>" on a place NP, and a mass constant has no witness to carry an entity-side position atom, leaving two co-equal Location atoms as the only route.

Agent-nominalization with an of-phrase ("the keepers of the Harbor Row"): it passes the nominalization-oblique rule's verb-paraphrase test but falls outside that rule's stated scope (act/result/quality nouns), while the Possession genitive is scoped to relational nouns with no underlying verb.
new_gaps: Anaphoric "that night" in a multi-day / multi-strand narrative: when the recency-salient antecedent event is itself day-unanchored, term propagation degrades to the bare day-part and nothing records that the night belongs to the day just narrated — a licensed form would need to tie a day-part to an antecedent EVENT rather than to copied calendar terms.
adjudication.notes: One atom the reviewer did not raise and I do not confirm as a defect: (Member sk_mire_essence_1 stored), from the prenominal participle in "the stored mire-essence", is emitted unwrapped while a past host clause wraps an appositive's typing atom — the instruction set names appositives, not restrictive participial modifiers, so it is unsettled rather than wrong, and the parse is at least consistent with its fallen/ground handling. Everything else independently checks out: the partitive shape for "thirty of the fallen feathers", the "by evening" TimeAtMost bound, the silken-vs-clay modifier-genus split, the Around/Against surface-preposition obliques, clean witness indexing, and the strength-0 distributing rule with its "no" QuantifierPhrase companion.
